doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Ray Charles and the shelved album
title: Ray Charles invites him to California
summary: Via Joe Adams, Ray wants to record him; for the first time he is allowed to pick tunes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Just kind of moving on a little bit here: tell us how we get into this next period of your music, that you meet Ray Charles. Did you meet him through Mary Ann?
No.
Or had you known him before?
No, no. What it was, I had . . .
This was like 1958, 1959-ish, end of the ’50s.
Yeah. You see, we all traveled. They were travelling too. We’d meet up in different towns, and I got to know Ray. Then he got Adams – Joe Adams . . .
Yeah, became his manager.
. . . became – he gave him a job as his manager.
Right, early 1960s now.
Uh-huh. Anyway, then he told Joe to have me come to California. He wanted to record me.
Before that, did you know that Ray was a Jimmy Scott enthusiast, a fan of yours?
No, I didn’t.
So all the times you’re hanging out, the times that you had met him on . . .
Right.
. . . the road, he never told you, “Man, I love the way you sing.” You just didn’t have any idea.
Oh. He respected me, and I always found him to be a very generous person. With all the artists that he dealt with, he was a generous person.
So you get a call from Joe Adams that says, Ray wants you to come to California.
That I – that Ray wants to record me.
So you go to California.
I go to California. We started rehearsing at his house.
Were you instrumental – a bad pun – did you help pick out the tunes?
Oh yeah. He was glad that I wanted to do those tunes. He had intended that we would continue. He passed before we could get together.
But, just keep it on this little time zone, for a while. So this is really, if we look at the big recording career of Jimmy Scott, beginning with Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool and Roost and Savoy . . .
Yeah, I finally get . . .
This is the first time . . .
Yeah.
. . . you got – someone was telling you, you tell me what you want to sing.
That’s right.
You bring me some songs.
